guides.title: Raw source data
guides.purpose: This directory holds user-supplied licensed inputs, downloaded source archives, editable foreground scenario files, and allocated carrying capacity (aCC) inputs.
inputs: Scenario and aCC templates installed by `set_workspace`.
Licensed ecoinvent archives and complete aCC results supplied by the user.
Public sources downloaded by `download_data` and premise IAM files downloaded by `prepare_backgrounds`.

expected_contents.name: foreground_scenarios/
expected_contents.description: default inputs, schemas, authoring templates, and runnable YAML scenarios

expected_contents.name: ecoinvent/
expected_contents.description: licensed ecoinvent 3.12 archives, extracted LCIA workbook, source manifest, and adjacent guide

expected_contents.name: remind_mfa/
expected_contents.description: REMIND-MFA 0.2.0 code and input data 1.0.0 archives with their source manifest and guide

expected_contents.name: pb_lcia/
expected_contents.description: AESA PB-LCIA source archive, source manifest, and guide

expected_contents.name: premise/
expected_contents.description: premise IAM files downloaded for each prepared background scenario

expected_contents.name: allocated_cc/
expected_contents.description: allocated carrying capacity templates and complete results

expected_contents.name: methodological_notes/
expected_contents.description: article and Methodological appendix PDFs, per-unit LCI workbook, and citation guide

tables_and_schemas: Each child guide names the applicable manifest or schema.
units_signs_and_identifiers: Source archives preserve their native bytes and units.
Folder names use readable source or workflow names; hashes remain inside manifests.
guides.pandas_example:
import pandas as pd

defaults = pd.read_parquet(
    workspace / "data_raw/foreground_scenarios/default_inputs/default_input_values.parquet"
)
reuse_and_refresh: Each workflow's guide describes its refresh scope.
scientific_limitations: Raw files provide the sources for subsequent processing and calculations.
The user supplies licensed ecoinvent content locally.

guides.title: Methodological documentation
guides.purpose: This directory contains the per-unit life cycle inventory (LCI) workbook, citation guidance, and article and Methodological appendix PDFs.

expected_contents.name: LCI_per_unit.xlsx
expected_contents.description: per-unit inventory quantities, provider identifiers, equations, source references, and reading guidance

expected_contents.name: pytoce_article.pdf
expected_contents.description: article PDF

expected_contents.name: pytoce_methodological_appendix.pdf
expected_contents.description: Methodological appendix PDF

expected_contents.name: recommended_citations.txt
expected_contents.description: software, data, and methodological citations

tables_and_schemas: The workbook's Read me sheet explains its linked inventory and source tables; each table retains its quantity basis and provenance.
units_signs_and_identifiers: Inventory quantities retain the reference units and process boundaries stated in the workbook.
guides.pandas_example:
import pandas as pd

workbook = pd.ExcelFile(workspace / "data_raw/methodological_notes/LCI_per_unit.xlsx")
print(workbook.sheet_names)
reuse_and_refresh: `set_workspace` installs missing documentation and preserves existing files by default.
`set_workspace(refresh=True)` restores package-named documentation files along with the other packaged workspace files; files with other names are preserved.
scientific_limitations: The workbook documents the model's life cycle inventories.
Reproduction of the referenced native exchange vectors requires separately licensed ecoinvent inputs.
The workbook's Sources and Source uses sheets link the quantities to their references.

guides.title: Reusable processed calculation inputs
guides.purpose: This directory holds reusable inputs produced from raw sources for MFA, LCA, monitoring ASR, and optimization.
inputs: Compiled foreground scenarios, extracted REMIND-MFA files, prepared Brightway backgrounds, processed allocated carrying capacity (aCC) results, and response tables.

expected_contents.name: ecoinvent/
expected_contents.description: plastics recipe derived locally from licensed EcoSpold inputs

expected_contents.name: foreground_scenarios/
expected_contents.description: compiled annual foreground-scenario inputs

expected_contents.name: remind_mfa/
expected_contents.description: extracted REMIND-MFA 0.2.0 execution source

expected_contents.name: brightway/
expected_contents.description: dependency-controlled Brightway storage

expected_contents.name: prepared_backgrounds/
expected_contents.description: shared and background-specific prospective LCA data

expected_contents.name: allocated_cc/
expected_contents.description: processed aCC results

expected_contents.name: optimization_response_bank/
expected_contents.description: reusable environmental responses for optimization

tables_and_schemas: Each processed product records its schema, source identities, and input hashes in its completion file.
units_signs_and_identifiers: Scientific tables use their declared native or model units.
Readable foreground and background names identify child directories.
guides.pandas_example:
import pandas as pd

compiled = pd.read_parquet(
    workspace / "data_processed/foreground_scenarios/remind_mfa_default/compiled_annual_input_parameters.parquet"
)
reuse_and_refresh: Completed children are selected by readable directory name and manifest existence.
Check the creating workflow's guide for its supported refresh options and scope.
scientific_limitations: Processed inputs support the subsequent MFA, LCA, and ASR calculations.
Manage Brightway's internal directory through Brightway's own operations.

guides.title: Scientific results
guides.purpose: This directory contains completed MFA, LCA, monitoring ASR, and optimization results for each foreground scenario.
inputs: Completed foreground scenarios, REMIND-MFA sources, selected prepared backgrounds, and processed allocated carrying capacity (aCC) results when optimization is requested.

expected_contents.name: <foreground_scenario>/
expected_contents.description: one readable scenario directory containing `mfa_results/` and, when requested, `lca_results/`, `asr_results/`, and `optimization_results/`

tables_and_schemas: Each result directory has its own manifest and adjacent guide.
units_signs_and_identifiers: Units are explicit in result tables.
Directory names use the readable foreground scenario; content hashes are stored in manifests.
guides.pandas_example:
import pandas as pd

scores = pd.read_parquet(
    workspace / "results/remind_mfa_default/lca_results/<selection>/scores.parquet"
)
reuse_and_refresh: Public workflows reuse a completed result when its manifest exists.
After changing an input under the same name, use `refresh=True` on the workflow that creates the result.
scientific_limitations: Results are valid only for the inputs and methods recorded in their manifests.
Global values are derived from the 12 regional results.

guides.title: Foreground scenario inputs
guides.purpose: This directory contains the versioned parameter catalog and all YAML materials used to write prospective plastics scenarios.
inputs: REMIND-MFA SSP2 defaults and parameter definitions supplied with the package.
YAML files placed by the user only in `scenarios/`.

expected_contents.name: default_inputs/
expected_contents.description: machine-readable parameter catalog and annual default values

expected_contents.name: schemas/
expected_contents.description: JSON contracts for scenario and result structures

expected_contents.name: templates/
expected_contents.description: non-runnable templates, examples, annual CSV view, and focused authoring guide

expected_contents.name: scenarios/
expected_contents.description: the sole runnable scenario-discovery directory

tables_and_schemas: `default_inputs/default_input_values.parquet` supplies coordinate-level defaults; `schemas/foreground_scenario_schema_v1.json` defines YAML structure.
units_signs_and_identifiers: Each parameter's unit, bounds, role, dimensions, and valid modes are in `default_inputs/parameter_catalogue.json`.
guides.pandas_example:
import pandas as pd

defaults = pd.read_parquet(
    workspace / "data_raw/foreground_scenarios/default_inputs/default_input_values.parquet"
)
reuse_and_refresh: `set_workspace(refresh=True)` restores package files and preserves user templates and scenarios whose filenames differ from the packaged files.
After editing a runnable YAML under the same name, use `run_mfa(foreground_scenario="your_name", refresh=True)` or choose a new name.
scientific_limitations: History through 2019 is immutable for ordinary foreground scenarios.
Scenarios use `SSP2`; the MFA calculates the derived outputs from the authored inputs.

guides.title: Default annual foreground inputs
guides.purpose: This directory provides the parameter catalog and complete annual default values used before MFA execution.
inputs: REMIND-MFA input data 1.0.0 for SSP2, packaged with pyToCE.

expected_contents.name: parameter_catalogue.json
expected_contents.description: roles, dimensions, modes, constraints, dependencies, and provenance for every foreground parameter

expected_contents.name: default_input_values.parquet
expected_contents.description: complete annual default input values at applicable coordinates

expected_contents.name: default_input_values_manifest.json
expected_contents.description: REMIND-MFA source, Zenodo DOI, CC-BY-SA-4.0 license, and exact table provenance

tables_and_schemas: The Parquet table contains parameter, year, applicable coordinates, unit, role, and default value; the JSON catalog defines parameter semantics.
units_signs_and_identifiers: Units are parameter-specific and explicit; shares are fractions.
Parameter IDs and coordinates match the machine-readable catalog exactly.
guides.pandas_example:
import pandas as pd

defaults = pd.read_parquet(
    workspace / "data_raw/foreground_scenarios/default_inputs/default_input_values.parquet"
)
print(defaults.query("parameter_id == 'collection_rate'").head())
reuse_and_refresh: Scenario compilation reads these package defaults when creating a new compiled result.
scientific_limitations: These files supply scenario inputs and fixed references for the MFA.
Default stocks and flows are produced by `run_mfa`.
The compact default table remains CC-BY-SA-4.0 material derived from the REMIND-MFA input-data release identified by the adjacent manifest.

guides.title: Foreground and MFA schemas
guides.purpose: This directory exposes the versioned machine-readable contracts for scenario inputs, compiled annual inputs, and MFA result artifacts.
inputs: Schema resources supplied with the package and used by the scenario compiler and MFA calculation.

expected_contents.name: foreground_scenario_schema_v1.json
expected_contents.description: runnable YAML scenario structure with scalar and grouped trajectories

expected_contents.name: compiled_annual_input_parameters_schema_v1.json
expected_contents.description: compiled 2020-2100 input-table contract

expected_contents.name: mfa_result_schema_v1.json
expected_contents.description: files and tables in a completed MFA result

tables_and_schemas: Each JSON file defines one v1 structure; the template guide explains how to write a scenario.
units_signs_and_identifiers: YAML values use the units defined in the parameter catalog. Compiled and result tables record units; technical field names remain stable `snake_case` identifiers.
guides.pandas_example:
import pandas as pd

schema = pd.read_json(
    workspace / "data_raw/foreground_scenarios/schemas/foreground_scenario_schema_v1.json",
    typ="series",
)
reuse_and_refresh: Schemas are installed once and restored by `set_workspace(refresh=True)`.
These schemas describe the file structure. `run_mfa` also checks scenario values and mass-balance feasibility.
scientific_limitations: Schemas check the input file structure. `run_mfa` checks values and the feasibility of the resulting stocks and flows.

guides.title: Foreground scenario examples
guides.purpose: This directory contains focused, non-runnable YAML examples for each legal foreground-scenario syntax family.
inputs: Examples supplied with the package and aligned with the parameter catalog and `README_foreground_scenarios.md`.

expected_contents.name: 01_stock_volume.yaml
expected_contents.description: stock trajectory syntax

expected_contents.name: 02_lifetime.yaml
expected_contents.description: conditional lifetime change points

expected_contents.name: 03_plastic_family_mix.yaml
expected_contents.description: new-inflow material composition

expected_contents.name: 04_circularity_treatment.yaml
expected_contents.description: collection and complete treatment shares, including landfill

expected_contents.name: 05_virgin_feedstock.yaml
expected_contents.description: fossil, biogenic, and DACCU feedstock shares

expected_contents.name: 06_waste_trade.yaml
expected_contents.description: balanced regional waste-trade changes

expected_contents.name: 07_socioeconomic_drivers.yaml
expected_contents.description: supported socioeconomic-driver syntax

tables_and_schemas: All files follow `../../schemas/foreground_scenario_schema_v1.json`; exact defaults remain in `../../default_inputs/default_input_values.parquet`.
units_signs_and_identifiers: Example values use each parameter's catalog unit and readable world region/material/good coordinates.
Examples demonstrate the supported scenario syntax.
guides.pandas_example:
import pandas as pd

defaults = pd.read_parquet(
    workspace / "data_raw/foreground_scenarios/default_inputs/default_input_values.parquet"
)
reuse_and_refresh: Copy an example to `../../scenarios/` before editing.
Package refresh restores the packaged examples and preserves user files with other names.
scientific_limitations: Example intervention values illustrate the scenario input format.

guides.title: Runnable foreground scenarios
guides.purpose: This is the only directory from which executable foreground scenarios are selected.
inputs: Complete YAML definitions copied from templates or authored under the documented schema.

expected_contents.name: remind_mfa_default.yaml
expected_contents.description: REMIND-MFA default scenario inputs with pyToCE constituent processing and recovery

expected_contents.name: frozen_2019_default_baseline.yaml
expected_contents.description: 2019frozen_SSP2demand, the publication-facing name of the baseline that follows default non-controls while holding regional 2019 collection, complete treatment composition and virgin feedstock composition until intervention

expected_contents.name: <foreground_scenario>.yaml
expected_contents.description: optional user-authored scenario whose stem matches `foreground_scenario`

tables_and_schemas: Runnable files follow `../schemas/foreground_scenario_schema_v1.json`; the templates guide documents ordinary change points and grouped linear trajectories.
units_signs_and_identifiers: Values use catalog units and explicit coordinates; readable filenames use lowercase `snake_case`.
Shares are fractions and complete partitions must close exactly.
guides.pandas_example:
import pandas as pd

defaults = pd.read_parquet(
    workspace / "data_raw/foreground_scenarios/default_inputs/default_input_values.parquet"
)
reuse_and_refresh: `run_mfa` selects a completed readable-name result by its completion manifest.
After changing a YAML under the same name, call `run_mfa(foreground_scenario="your_name", refresh=True)` or use a new readable name.
scientific_limitations: 2019frozen_SSP2demand retains SSP2-driven default stock demand, lifetimes, end-use material composition and trade propensities. Its runtime identifier remains `frozen_2019_default_baseline`. Mechanical recovery and its air, water and managed solid losses use fixed constituent recipes; recycling allocation respects available receiving demand.
